title: Household Add-On Membership: how the sibling discount and the household bundle discount combine
content:
## Product and scope
This document states the Household Add-On Membership basis for selecting the discount rate applied to a dues charge when a primary member holds more than one household add-on.

## Rule
Each dependent add-on beyond the primary member's first is eligible for that tier's sibling discount rate off the tier's monthly dues. Once the primary member's number of open household add-ons (of any tier) reaches that tier's household multi-add-on minimum count, every one of the primary member's open add-ons instead becomes eligible for that tier's household multi-add-on bundle discount rate. Where both a sibling discount rate and a bundle discount rate would apply to the same add-on, only the higher of the two rates is applied to that add-on's dues charge; the two rates are never added together or applied one after the other on top of each other.

## Points of judgement
- The sibling discount rate looks only at whether a given add-on is the primary member's first of that tier or an additional one; the bundle discount rate looks instead at the total count of open household add-ons across every tier the primary member holds.
- Reaching the household multi-add-on minimum count changes which single discount rate applies to every open add-on, not only to the add-on that caused the count to be reached.
- "Whichever is higher" governs the selection: if a tier's sibling discount rate happens to exceed that tier's bundle discount rate for a given add-on, the sibling rate is the one applied once the comparison is made, and the bundle rate is not layered on top of it.

## Hypothetical case (illustrative only)
Suppose a primary member's open household add-ons have not yet reached the household multi-add-on minimum count for their tier, and one of those add-ons is not the primary member's first of its tier. That add-on's dues charge is discounted at its tier's sibling discount rate. If the primary member later opens enough additional household add-ons that the count reaches the household multi-add-on minimum, every one of the primary member's open add-ons is thereafter discounted at its own tier's household multi-add-on bundle discount rate instead of the sibling rate, because the bundle rate governs once the count threshold is reached, and the two rates are not stacked.

The sibling discount rate, the household multi-add-on minimum count and the bundle discount rate in force for each add-on tier are recorded in that tier's own parameter basis.
